growth_signal.value: Plans to manufacture up to 200 satellites a year and now operates bases in the UK, Spain, Portugal and Greece, working with customers like AWS.

entry.idea: Open Cosmos builds and launches small satellites for governments and businesses that want their own space missions without building everything from scratch.
entry.lesson: Turn a very expensive, custom process, like building a satellite, into a repeatable, semi-standard product, and sell it to many customers.
entry.name: Open Cosmos

growth.basis: substitute: a funding round bigger than the last, plus stated plans to scale to 200 satellites a year
growth.reason: No revenue or satellite count numbers were found; the clearest signal is a very large new funding round and expansion plans.

market.reason: Satellite services are needed by governments and businesses worldwide, and independence from foreign satellite networks is a growing priority.

tech.reason: Building and mass-manufacturing satellites at scale is hard engineering that few companies can do well.

sources.title: Open Cosmos, a UK satellite startup focused on sustainability, raises $50M | TechCrunch
UK-headquartered satellite startup Open Cosmos plans European rival to Starlink - Tech.eu
Open Cosmos fires up its satellite ambitions with €300M

entry.twist: It aims to mass-manufacture up to 200 satellites a year to offer Europe an independent alternative to systems like Starlink.
entry.who_pays: Space agencies, governments and companies pay for satellite missions and access to Open Cosmos's satellite technology.
entry.why_now: Governments and companies want space capability that is not dependent on a single foreign provider, and satellite costs keep falling.
